title: Fast Algorithms for Stoquastic Spin Systems
abstract: We establish a general framework for developing fast sampling and counting algorithms for stoquastic spin systems at high temperature. Our framework is based on a rapidly mixing Markov chain for polymer models and a subcritical percolation process for sampling individual polymers. We apply our framework to obtain fast algorithms for approximating the partition function and sampling from the thermal distribution of (1) general stoquastic spin systems, (2) ferromagnetic Heisenberg models, and (3) antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models on bipartite graphs. For the Heisenberg models, we obtain an improved bound on the inverse temperature by using their respective cycle and loop representations.
summary: This paper presents a general framework to develop fast algorithms for sampling and counting in stoquastic spin systems at high temperatures. By mapping the quantum problem onto a graphlet polymer model, the authors achieve efficient computational bounds for calculating the partition function and sampling the thermal state. This methodology is successfully applied to Heisenberg spin models, providing significant algorithmic advances in quantum statistical mechanics.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop fast and efficient algorithms for both sampling and counting observables associated with stoquastic spin systems at high temperatures.
main_result: Fast algorithms are established for approximating the partition function and sampling the thermal distribution for general stoquastic spin systems, as well as for ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Heisenberg models on bipartite graphs.
method: The approach combines a general framework based on rapidly mixing Markov chains for polymer models with graphlet sampling algorithms, utilizing probabilistic extensions for computational tractability.
model_or_system: The focus is on stoquastic spin systems defined by a Hamiltonian $H_S = \sum_{e \in E(G)} \Phi(e)$ on a graph $G$. Specific applications include Heisenberg models (ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic) on bipartite graphs.
key_observables: The partition function $Z_S = 	ext{Tr}(e^{- eta H_S})$ and the thermal state $ho_S$, from which the thermal distribution $\mu_{ho_S}(\sigma)$ is derived.
important_parameters: High temperature ($ eta$ small), the graph structure $G$, and the inverse temperature $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The framework relies on the stoquastic condition (non-positive matrix elements) and the assumption that the underlying polymer model is $\kappa$-computable.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework using polymer dynamics and graphlet sampling. It then applies this framework to derive fast algorithms for general stoquastic systems and specific Heisenberg models, culminating in the proof of tractability via probabilistic polymer models.
why_interesting: The development of fast, polynomial-time classical algorithms for sampling and counting in quantum spin systems, especially those with non-negative weight structures, is highly relevant for simulating complex many-body quantum models.
